learning.title: The secrets key id is bound into every ciphertext; there is no in-place key rotation
learning.trigger: Replacing or relabelling BAKERY_SECRETS_KEY_B64, BAKERY_SECRETS_KEY_ID or the mounted secrets key file, or restoring a database onto a host that holds a different key.
learning.mistake: Treated the secrets key as a rotatable environment value, changed the key or the id in place, and left every stored credential (object-storage credentials, integration secrets) undecryptable.
learning.rule: Stored credentials are AES-GCM payloads bound to the secret id, its revision and BAKERY_SECRETS_KEY_ID. Changing the key bytes or the id makes every existing credential unreadable. Treat the id as immutable once any credential exists. To rotate: use a new id and a new key and re-enter the credentials through the product; never edit ciphertext rows or relabel the id.

The key must be exactly 32 bytes (invalid base64 or length exits 78 SECRETS_KEY_INVALID, value never printed); without a key, credential writes are disabled and saves answer 409. Back up the key and its id together with the database: a restored database without its original key and id holds unreadable credentials.

verification.requirement: After any deliberate key change or restore, re-run a product check that decrypts a stored credential (for example Verify connection on the object-storage settings) and record the fixed result code. Never print the key or a credential.

learning.boundary: The entrypoint writes the key to a mode 0600 file and unsets the environment variable; do not read it back from the environment of a running process.
